query: (Cathay MD) Build a model to organise/optimise routes and service so Overall Rating > 7.

per_column.name: primary_service_complaint_category
per_column.rationale: Gives a strong grouping axis for identifying which service failure areas drive low ratings, directly serving route/service optimization. Categories are well-grounded in review text (ground_service, operational_disruption, crew_service all match samples). One mismatch: a praise-only review labeled 'crew_service' as complaint is questionable but the crew is the dominant topic, so tolerable.

per_column.name: customer_service_responsiveness
per_column.rationale: A useful behavioral axis distinct from complaint category; captures responsiveness pattern that maps to actionable service fixes. Values are sound readings of text (unresponsive_post_incident, proactive_attentive, staff_rushing_no_downtime all warranted by samples).

per_column.name: ground_service_failure_signal
per_column.rationale: A bare boolean flag that is largely redundant with primary_service_complaint_category's ground_service value, reducing its independent analytical leverage. However values are well-grounded and correctly extracted from text.

per_column.name: service_quality_trend_signal
per_column.rationale: The concept (trend/root-cause signal) would help strategic optimization, but several produced values are unsupported inferences. 'cost_cutting_visible' for a diversion/no-help incident, 'understaffing' for a gate-change delay, 'pre_covid_premium_lost' and 'infrastructure_aging' for positive reviews with no temporal or cost cues are invented specifics the text does not support.

per_column.name: cabin_class_expectation_gap
per_column.rationale: Class-vs-expectation gap is a genuine axis for service optimization by cabin. Values track the Class column and text reasonably (economy_meets_baseline, business_class_food_gap warranted; 'Unknown' correctly used for silent rows). Mild risk of asserting gaps beyond text but samples are defensible.

per_column.name: traveler_type_satisfaction_variance
per_column.rationale: Segmenting satisfaction by traveler type is useful and 'Type of Traveller' exists in source, but the produced values are frequently ungrounded: 'business_high_expectations' and 'family_young_kids_challenge' assigned to reviews with no stated traveler type, kids, or business context. These are invented specifics that likely contradict or overreach the source.

judge.rationale: The added columns collectively offer several genuine new axes (complaint category, responsiveness, class expectation gap) that directly support building a route/service optimization model targeting Overall Rating > 7. Groundedness is uneven: extraction-oriented columns are sound, but the inference-heavy columns (service_quality_trend_signal, traveler_type_satisfaction_variance) fabricate confident specifics—understaffing, cost-cutting, business/family traveler labels—not supported by the sampled source text, dragging overall groundedness down.
